newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian ex-communists get up to 20 years jail.
newsitem.headline: Albanian ex-communists get up to 20 years jail.

text.p: An Albanian court sentenced nine senior communist-era officials to prison for up to 20 years on Saturday for human rights abuses.
Judge Mehdi Bici found the nine ex-communists guilty of crimes against humanity for ordering thousands of dissidents into internal exile. Genocide charges were dropped.

Llambi Gegprifti, head of the communist party in the capital Tirana until the Stalinist government collapsed in 1990, was sentenced to 20 years, as were two officials of the secret police agency Sigurimi. The others got 15 to 16 years.

Around 100,000 Albanians are believed to have been forced into exile in remote villages during 45 years of communist rule, for allegedly expressing opinions against the Stalinist government or trying to escape from the isolated state.
The defence argued the defendants "simply applied the law of the time", but Bici said the trial had proved they had violated "constitutional human rights and freedom".

Three senior ex-communists were sentenced to death in May but an appeals court revoked the sentences and imposed jail terms instead. Thirteen other ex-communists have been sentenced to up to 25 years in jail for crimes against humanity.
No date has yet been set for the trial of former president Ramiz Alia and two former ministers charged with ordering the shooting of Albanians who tried to flee the country.
